content.text: Other Area WorkSource Workshops & Events -Virtual and Other Locations

list: Nov. 2: Job Fair Preparation, Virtual, 2:00-4:00pm. The Job Fair Prep Workshop equips participants with the knowledge, tools, and confidence needed to succeed at career fairs and networking events. Attendees learn how to create a strong professional introduction, tailor their resume, research employers, and communicate their skills effectively. The workshop covers networking strategies, professional appearance, interview preparation, and follow-up techniques that help candidates stand out to recruiters. Participants gain practical tips for navigating employer conversations, asking insightful questions, and making positive first impressions. Whether seeking a first job, career change, or advancement opportunity, this interactive workshop helps job seekers maximize connections and improve employment outcomes.

Nov. 4: Self-Employment Assistance Program(SEAP), 10:00am-11:30am, virtual. Ever thought about starting your own a business? If you are currently collecting unemployment the Self‐Employment Assistance Program (SEAP) may be a great training opportunity for you! If your application is approved you: • Receive business training. • Do not have to look for work while you are in training. • Can create a job that interests you. • May be able to provide jobs for others. All approved programs include: • Business training and counseling. • Technical help to set up, market and run a business (for example, setting up a business accounting system). • Activities related to setting up a business and becoming self-employed.

Sept. 23: Beyond Service: Unlocking Education Benefits for Veterans & Eligible Dependents, in person, 10:00am-11:00am. Navigate your path to higher education with our expert-led workshop that empowers veterans to transition successfully into college life while helping veterans, families, and eligible dependents make informed decisions about their educational future. Most veterans are aware that they are entitled to the Post 9/11 GI Bill for their education once they leave service. Many may have enlisted as a means to pay for college. Upon admission to their institution of choice, some have very little knowledge of what they may be entitled to and the processes involved in securing or receiving their benefits. Veteran participants can learn about college exploration, admissions processes, and military-to-academic cultural transitions. Empowers veterans with comprehensive knowledge of and securing their VA education benefits. Dependents Education Assistance (Chapter 35) may assist with college or university expenses. Learn about VA and WA State education benefits for dependents of veterans who have a 100% disability rating or who have passed away as a result of service.

This workshop is open to students of all ages and veterans who are considering obtaining a degree.
